title: Gazpacho
subtitle: Andalusian chilled tomato and vegetable soup
excerpt: Spain's great summer soup: ripe tomatoes, red pepper, cucumber, garlic, and olive oil blended into a vivid, chilled liquid salad that is as refreshing as it is flavourful. Made without cooking, at the peak of summer.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gazpacho is a cold raw vegetable soup from Andalusia in southern Spain, with roots predating the arrival of the tomato in Europe; the earliest versions were a bread, oil, vinegar, and garlic mixture called 'ajo blanco'. The modern tomato-based version became established in the nineteenth century. Gazpacho is not cooked at any stage; the flavour comes entirely from the quality and ripeness of the vegetables, which must be at their peak in summer for the best result. The traditional method involves pounding the vegetables with a pestle and mortar; the modern blender version is the standard home method. The bread in traditional recipes thickens the soup and softens the acidity; it can be omitted for a gluten-free version. The soup must be well chilled and generously seasoned.

content.text: Use the ripest, most flavourful tomatoes available; supermarket winter tomatoes will produce a pale, watery result. Blend the soup in a powerful blender for a minimum of 2 minutes for the smoothest texture, then pass through a sieve if a very refined result is wanted. The soup needs a full night in the fridge to let the flavours develop fully.

items.preparation: crusts removed; torn; optional but traditional

content.text: Place all the vegetables, bread if using, olive oil, vinegar, and seasoning in a blender. Blend for at least 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Taste and adjust the seasoning and vinegar. The soup should be well seasoned; it will taste flatter when cold. Transfer to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Taste and re-season before serving. Serve in chilled bowls with a drizzle of extra olive oil and any garnishes you like: finely diced cucumber, red pepper, tomato, or croutons are all traditional.
